# Week 4 plan: Still Here

Hacktoberfest 2026 DEV challenge, Week 4 "Ghost in the Machine".
Deadline: Oct 31, 11:59 PM PDT = **Sun Nov 1, 12:29 PM IST**. Aim to publish by Sat Oct 31 night IST.
Challenge page: https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week4-2026-10-26
Research behind this plan: `WINNERS.md` (this folder) and `../hf26-track-stats.md`.

## The hook

Title: **"I wrote a program that only runs after I die"**

Still Here is a dead man's switch with an open model inside. Every week it asks me one
question: "Are you still here?" While I keep answering, it does nothing but listen and
keep notes. If I stop answering, it asks two people I trust to confirm. Only when both
say yes does it wake up: it gives each person the letter and the facts meant for them,
answers my family's practical questions from my own notes, and closes the accounts I
asked it to close.

Theme fit: it is literally a ghost in the machine (a program that acts for me after I am
gone), and it honors the past the Día de los Muertos way: the dead leave something for
the living.

Why open matters (the post's core argument): a program meant to run years after I die
cannot depend on a model a company may retire or reprice next year. The model that
answers my family is open-weight, so the release can run on any host, or on my
sister's laptop with the Wi-Fi off. My private notes never need a closed API at the
moment that matters.

## Rules we follow (from the research)

- Model writes, code decides. The model drafts and answers; code decides when anything
  is released, who sees what, and whether an answer is backed by a note.
- One real person, one real moment, in the first two lines of the post.
- Honest numbers and a "what went wrong" section.
- A live link with no sign-up for a demo vault, a GIF at the top, a short video.
- Each partner track gets a real job, its own short section, and a measured result.
  No kitchen sink.
- Repo must be new (started Oct 27, inside the window).

## Tracks

Strategy: strong post first; then use as many thin tracks as genuinely fit, because each
track must pick a winner and a thin pool raises our odds. One post can win only once.

| Track | Week 3 entries | Job in Still Here |
|---|---|---|
| Ultramarine (Paper Instruments) | 12 | While I am alive: reads my documents (policies, statements, subscription emails) and writes the "what my family needs to know" handbook (.docx). The post states what the run cost. |
| Entire | 24 | The Claude Code sessions behind the repo, captured with the Entire CLI and linked in the post. |
| Auth0 for AI Agents | 25 | My sign-in; CIBA push approval to 2 trusted people before release; fine-grained authorization (Auth0 FGA) so each person can only retrieve their own letters and notes. |
| Backboard | 29 | Memory across check-ins: each "still here" answer can carry a line ("moved my FD to SBI"), and Backboard keeps the facts current, replacing stale ones. |
| Tiger Data | 30 | Main database: vault, check-ins, release state, audit log; hybrid BM25 + vector search over notes for family questions. |
| Browserbase | 32 | After release: closes accounts and cancels subscriptions on demo sites with Stagehand, one screenshot per step. Only if free browser time is left. |

Dropped: .tech (needs a card; do not suggest it again), SerpApi, Temporal, Mastra,
and the crowded ones (Gemma, Render, Copilot, Sentry, TabPFN, ElevenLabs, MongoDB).
Arduino, DigitalOcean, Tinker: not possible (no board / card / credits).

## How it works

States: `alive` -> `missed` (no answer to N check-ins) -> `confirming` (CIBA sent to
trusted people) -> `released`. Any check-in from me at any point resets to `alive`.

1. **Check-ins.** A daily job (Vercel cron) sends "Are you still here?" through ntfy.sh
   push with a one-tap link. Answering resets the clock. An optional free-text line goes
   to Backboard memory. Demo mode squeezes a week into a minute.
2. **Missed.** After N missed check-ins and a final "last chance" ping, the state moves
   to `confirming`.
3. **Confirming.** Auth0 CIBA sends each trusted person a Guardian push: "Anish has not
   answered for 3 weeks. Approve only if you know he has died." Both must approve. One
   deny, or my own check-in, cancels everything.
4. **Released.** Code (not the model) unlocks, per person, what FGA allows:
   - their letter (written by me, with the open model only helping me draft),
   - the handbook section meant for them (from Ultramarine + Backboard facts),
   - "Ask Anish's notes": the person asks "where is the LIC policy?"; hybrid search
     on Tiger returns only notes FGA allows for that person; the open model answers
     only from those notes with citations; code checks each cited note id exists and is
     allowed, otherwise it shows "He didn't leave a note about that."
   - Browserbase jobs for the accounts I listed, each logged with a screenshot.
5. **Audit.** Every step is written to an append-only log on Tiger and shown on a
   timeline page.

The model never decides anything. It never writes in my voice to the living (no
griefbot). It only helps me draft while I am alive and answers from my notes after.

## Stack

- Next.js on Vercel, bun. Auth0 Next.js SDK.
- Open model: gpt-oss-20b / 120b on Groq free tier for the live site (open weights,
  swappable through one OpenAI-compatible base URL), plus a local path (llama.cpp or
  Ollama with a small Qwen/Llama) to show the release running offline.
- Embeddings: in the browser or a small open embedding model (as in ReplyDesk).
- Tiger Data free service (pg_textsearch BM25 + pgvector/vectorscale).
- Auth0 tenant from Week 3 (CIBA trial ends around Nov 14) with a new application;
  Auth0 FGA if its free tier needs no card, else our own access table (weaker for the track).
- Ultramarine `ultramarine-1-flash` at `https://api.paperinstruments.com/v1`, $5 promo credit.
- Backboard memory (free credit covers Memory and RAG, not chat).
- Browserbase + Stagehand (free: 1 browser hour a month; check what is left).
- ntfy.sh for check-in pushes.

## What to measure (for the post)

- Family Q&A on a set of ~40 test questions over my real-shaped notes: answered with a
  valid citation, correctly said "no note", wrong. Open model sizes compared.
- FGA leak test: questions from person A that target person B's notes; must be 0 leaks.
- Ultramarine handbook run: tokens and exact cost.
- Backboard: how many stale facts were replaced across check-ins.
- Browserbase: jobs done, steps, browser minutes used.

## Schedule (IST)

- **Tue Oct 27 (tonight):** plan, repo, Entire set up, accounts and keys, schema.
- **Wed Oct 28:** state machine + check-ins + CIBA release; vault and letters; family
  Q&A with hybrid search and FGA. Three design options for the user to pick (design stop).
- **Thu Oct 29:** Ultramarine handbook, Backboard memory, Browserbase jobs, build the
  picked design.
- **Fri Oct 30:** deploy to Vercel, full real run with phone approvals, eval numbers.
  Week 3 results come out.
- **Sat Oct 31:** demo video (/demo-video), POST.md, user publishes. Buffer: Sun morning.

## Ultramarine: in (Oct 27)

The promo invite code from hacktoberfest.com/my/promos worked: access plus $5 credit.
Key goes in `week4/.env` as `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`. The track is in from the start.
Keep $5 in mind: cap `max_completion_tokens` on every call and log cost per run.
Design notes kept from the waitlist plan:

- All model calls go through one small client module with an OpenAI-compatible base URL
  and model name per job (`draft`, `answer`, `handbook`). Ultramarine is just another
  entry there.
- The handbook job (read documents, write the "what my family needs to know" file) is
  built first on the open model. If a key arrives, run the same job on Ultramarine,
  log tokens and cost per run, and compare both outputs side by side in the post.
- Keep a `usage` table on Tiger (job, model, input/output tokens, cost) from day one,
  so the "what the run cost" number is ready.
## Open items

- Done: Entire CLI installed and hooked to Claude Code (config committed), GitHub repo
  https://github.com/Sarcastic-Soul/still-here pushed. Build in a new Claude Code
  session opened inside the repo so Entire captures it.
- `week4/.env` made, with Groq, Backboard, Auth0 domain and Browserbase keys copied from
  week2/week3. Ultramarine key tested Oct 27 (22 tokens, about $0.000005). Tiger service `still-here` (gz32xb2thz, free) created Oct 27 and its `DATABASE_URL` is in `.env`; pg_textsearch, vector and vectorscale are available.
- Second trusted person for the CIBA demo (a second Guardian account on the user's phone works).
- Check Auth0 FGA free tier and Browserbase hours left.

Constraints: no card on any service, 7.5 GiB RAM laptop, bun.
Autonomy (same as Week 2/3, confirmed Oct 27): create public repo under Sarcastic-Soul
and push, deploy to Vercel, sign up for and use free services without asking.

## 3. Tracks that seem to get few strong entries

Signs: a winner with few reactions, a thin or unfinished build, or a post that
barely uses the open AI.

- **Arduino (featured, $200).** Week 1's winner was a device still being built
  ("Now I'm building...") that barely mentions an open model. Week 2's winner

- **Entire.** The Weekend winner was the shortest of all (1,050 words).
- **GitHub Copilot.** Winners had 0-3 reactions. Two were entered "through the
  GitHub Actions route" (CI on every push), which is a low bar.
- **Temporal.** Winners had 0-2 reactions. The trick that wins is always the
  same: kill the worker mid-run and show it pick up where it left off.
- **.tech domain.** Cheap to add on top of a live site. Week 2's winner just
  hosted the app on it.
- **New in Week 4, no past winners at all: Auth0 for AI Agents, Browserbase,
  Ultramarine (Paper Instruments).** New tracks usually have the smallest pool.
- **Most crowded:** Gemma, DigitalOcean, Render and ElevenLabs. Almost everyone
  uses Gemma and lists these by default.

---

## 4. Lessons for a Week 4 entry that catches attention at once

Week 4 is already crowded. In the first day and a half there were about 100
entries tagged `hf26challenge`. Most are close copies of the six example ideas
in the announcement: about 15 haunted terminals ("Phantom Terminal",
"PhantomShell", "GhostShell", "NecroShell"), about 8 séances with a dead
language (COBOL, ALGOL), about 8 ofrendas or memory altars, and a handful of
ghost story generators. Several already use the "it won't invent memories of
the dead" angle (Marigold, Ofrenda, Chitthi, "a ghost that refuses to lie").

1. **Don't build one of the six example ideas as written.** Take the plain
   reading of the theme (spooky, or honoring the past) and find a small twist
   nobody else will have, the way "your run grows a song" or "the output is
   paper" did.
2. **Start with one real person and one real moment, in the first two lines.**
   For the Día de los Muertos side, the closest past winner is the
   sister-in-law's voice-note cookbook: a real family, real recordings, real
   thanks at the end. For the spooky side, a real scare from your own life.
3. **Make the title a sentence with a hook.** A real quote, a surprise or a
   number. Not "Ghost AI" or "Phantom Terminal".
4. **Show the moment it landed.** A screenshot of the real reply, a quote, a
   photo. The Week 4 template even has an optional "The Spirit of It" section for
   this. The judges asked for it, and most quick entries will skip it.
5. **Let the model write and let code decide, and prove it with numbers.** Test
   a few model sizes, count the errors, show one honest failure. Most Week 4
   entries so far are 2-4 minute reads with no numbers at all.
6. **Live link with no sign-up, plus a hero GIF at the top, plus a short
   video.** Every overall winner had a link that works in one click.
7. **Tie "why open matters" to this exact project.** Family photos and voices
   stay on your own machine; it works with the internet off; it won't vanish
   when a service shuts down. Show it (Wi-Fi off in the video), don't just say it.
8. **Aim for a thin track on purpose, and use it deeply.** Browserbase, Auth0
   for AI Agents, Ultramarine, Arduino or Temporal have small pools. One deep use
   (a section with a screenshot of it working) beats listing seven sponsors.

---

## 5. What to avoid

From the weak partner winners and the early Week 4 pool:

- **Bare product-name titles**: "Phantom AI", "GHOSTLY AI", "PhantomShell AI",
  "Ghost in the Machine." Many Week 4 titles are like this. Only 2 of 50 past
  winners had a name-only title, both in partner tracks with 1 reaction each.
- **Short posts.** No past winner was under about 1,050 words. Many Week 4 posts
  so far are 1-2 minute reads.
- **Leaving template comments** (`<!-- ... -->`) in the published post.
- **A theme sticker on an unrelated tool** (for example a migration checker or a
  token saver with "ghost" in the name). Winners make the theme the core of the
  product.
- **Big claims with no proof.** Winners show the eval, the trace, the crash test.
  "AI-powered" with no numbers reads as filler.
- **No real person.** "For everyone" posts did not win overall. Every overall
  winner was built for a named person or a clear small group.
- **Only a video, or only a GitHub link.** Judges like being able to click and
  try it.
- **Sponsor lists without depth.** Listing seven prize categories is fine, but
  only the ones with their own section and a screenshot won.

-- Still Here schema on Tiger Data (Postgres). Apply with: bun run db:schema
-- Safe to run again: every statement is IF NOT EXISTS / OR REPLACE.

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vectorscale;    -- DiskANN index
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_textsearch;  -- BM25 ranking

-- One vault per owner. The public demo runs on its own vault so it never touches the real one.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vaults (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  slug        text UNIQUE NOT NULL,                -- 'anish', 'demo'
  owner_name  text NOT NULL,
  is_demo     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- The owner and the people the owner trusts. Trusted people approve the release (CIBA)
-- and receive letters and notes. auth0_sub is filled the first time they sign in.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS people (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role        text NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('owner', 'trusted')),
  name        text NOT NULL,
  relation    text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',            -- 'sister', 'friend'
  email       text NOT NULL,
  auth0_sub   text,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (vault_id, email)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS people_sub_idx ON people (vault_id, auth0_sub) WHERE auth0_sub IS NOT NULL;

-- The switch itself. One row per vault.
-- alive -> missed -> confirming -> released. A check-in from the owner goes back to alive
-- from any state except released.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS switch (
  vault_id          uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  state             text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'alive' CHECK (state IN ('alive', 'missed', 'confirming', 'released')),
  every_seconds     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 604800,  -- one check-in a week; demo uses seconds
  miss_limit        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,       -- misses before the last-chance ping
  grace_seconds     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 172800,  -- time to answer the last-chance ping
  last_answer_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_ping_at      timestamptz,
  missed_count      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_chance_at    timestamptz,                      -- when the last-chance ping went out
  round             integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,       -- bumps every time confirming starts
  released_at       timestamptz,
  updated_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Every "Are you still here?" ping and its answer.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checkins (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind         text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'regular' CHECK (kind IN ('regular', 'last_chance')),
  sent_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  answered_at  timestamptz,
  line         text,                                -- optional free-text line, goes to memory
  channel      text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ntfy'
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS checkins_vault_idx ON checkins (vault_id, sent_at DESC);

-- One CIBA request per trusted person per confirming round.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approvals (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  person_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  round        integer NOT NULL,
  auth_req_id  text,                                -- null in demo mode (simulated approval)
  status       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'denied', 'expired', 'cancelled')),
  sent_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at   timestamptz,
  decided_at   timestamptz,
  UNIQUE (vault_id, person_id, round)
);

-- Letters the owner wrote. Who can read one is decided by Auth0 FGA, not by this table.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS letters (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  recipient_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title         text NOT NULL,
  body          text NOT NULL,
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- The owner's notes: the facts family members can ask about after release.
-- shared_with records the owner's choice; FGA tuples are written from it and are what
-- every read is checked against.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title        text NOT NULL,
  body         text NOT NULL,
  shared_with  uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',        -- people.id list
  search_text  text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (title || E'\n' || body) STORED,
  embedding    vector(384),                         -- BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5
  source       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'owner',       -- owner | checkin | memory
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS notes_vault_idx ON notes (vault_id);
-- Hybrid search: BM25 for exact words (policy numbers, bank names), DiskANN for meaning.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS notes_bm25_idx ON notes USING bm25 (search_text) WITH (text_config = 'english');
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS notes_embedding_idx ON notes USING diskann (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Documents the handbook job reads while the owner is alive (policies, statements,
-- subscription emails). Pasted or uploaded as text.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind        text NOT NULL,                        -- policy | statement | subscription | other
  title       text NOT NULL,
  body        text NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- The "what my family needs to know" handbook. One row per run, so runs can be compared.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS handbooks (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  model        text NOT NULL,
  sections     jsonb NOT NULL,                      -- [{audience, title, items: [{text, sources}]}]
  dropped      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',         -- items code removed (bad or missing sources)
  docx         bytea,
  usage_id     uuid,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Every model call: what job, which model, tokens and what it cost.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usage (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id          uuid REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  job               text NOT NULL,                  -- draft | answer | handbook | eval
  provider          text NOT NULL,                  -- groq | ultramarine | local
  model             text NOT NULL,
  input_tokens      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cached_tokens     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  output_tokens     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  reasoning_tokens  integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cost_usd          numeric(12, 8) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- list price; Groq free tier is billed $0
  latency_ms        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ok                boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS usage_job_idx ON usage (job, created_at DESC);

-- Questions family members asked after release, and what came back.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS questions (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  person_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  question     text NOT NULL,
  outcome      text NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('answered', 'no_note', 'refused')),
  answer       text NOT NULL,
  cited        uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  candidates   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,          -- notes search found
  allowed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,          -- of those, notes FGA let through
  usage_id     uuid,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Accounts to close after release (Browserbase jobs).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS closures (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  vault_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  site         text NOT NULL,
  url          text NOT NULL,
  instruction  text NOT NULL,
  status       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting' CHECK (status IN ('waiting', 'running', 'done', 'failed')),
  steps        jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',         -- [{action, screenshot_url, at}]
  session_id   text,
  browser_ms   integer,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Append-only audit log. Every step of the switch writes here; nothing may change it later.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
  id        bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  vault_id  uuid REFERENCES vaults(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  actor     text NOT NULL,                          -- system | owner | person:<id> | model
  action    text NOT NULL,
  detail    jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS audit_vault_idx ON audit_log (vault_id, at DESC);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION audit_log_append_only() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Deleting a whole vault (the demo reset) is the one allowed way rows go away.
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' AND current_setting('still_here.vault_reset', true) = 'on' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_log is append-only';
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS audit_log_no_change ON audit_log;
CREATE TRIGGER audit_log_no_change BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit_log
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_log_append_only();

# Design guardrails

The goal: every UI should look like a human designer made deliberate choices.
If a choice is the first thing any AI would pick, pick something else.

## 0. Pipeline (run this automatically, the user should not have to ask)

This skill is the entry point. When UI work starts, go through these steps in order:

1. **Direction** — do section 1 below. If `~/design-refs/` has screenshots, use them.
2. **Explore** — for a brand-new product, landing page or deck, build 3 clearly different
   hero directions as local static HTML files (`design-options/option-1.html` etc.), each
   with its own font, color and layout. Screenshot them if Playwright is available, and let
   the user pick one before building the rest. Skip for small changes and internal screens.
   Never use tools that need an account, login or credits.
3. **Build** — load `taste-skill` and pick the variant that fits the direction
   (`minimalist-skill`, `soft-skill`, `brutalist-skill`; `redesign-skill` when restyling
   an existing UI). Also follow `frontend-design`. Sections 2–4 of this file override
   both when they disagree.
4. **Check** — do section 5: screenshots, banned-list check, then a manual audit
   (contrast, focus, touch targets, responsive) and a polish pass.

For a small tweak to an existing UI (one component, a color fix), skip step 2 and
the full audit in step 4; still follow the banned list.

## 1. Pick a direction first

Before any code, write down in 3–5 lines:
- Who uses it and where (phone in a field, office desktop, student at night)
- One real-world reference for the feel (a newspaper, a train timetable, a lab notebook, a Swiss poster)
- Display font, body font, one accent color, neutral tone (warm or cool)
- What it must NOT look like

Match the domain:
- **Government / public service:** plain, calm, high-trust. Follow GOV.UK Design System / USWDS / India GIGW style. Big clear type, strong contrast, no decoration, no motion for show.
- **Farmers / rural users:** very large text and tap targets, icons next to every label, high contrast (used outdoors in sun), local-language ready, light pages for slow networks.
- **Ed-tech:** friendly and warm, progress and streaks visible, rounded but not childish. References: Duolingo, Khan Academy, Brilliant.
- **Dev tools / SaaS:** restrained, dense, precise. References: Linear, Vercel, Raycast.
- **Health / finance:** calm, trustworthy, lots of space, numbers easy to read.

If `~/design-refs/` exists, look at the screenshots there and pull colors, fonts and spacing from them.

## 2. Banned patterns

### Color
- Blue-to-purple, indigo-to-violet, or pink-to-orange gradients anywhere
- Gradient text on headings
- Glowing blurred blobs / orbs in the background
- Default Tailwind `indigo-500` / `violet-500` as the brand color
- Pure `#000` or `#fff` — tint neutrals slightly warm or cool
- More than one accent color
- Gray text on colored backgrounds
- Dark navy/slate background with neon accents as the default "techy" look

### Typography
- Inter, Roboto, Arial, Open Sans, or system font as the only font
- Every heading the same weight with no size contrast
- Tiny uppercase "eyebrow" pill badge above the hero (`✨ New: ...`)

### Layout
- Centered hero, then three identical feature cards with an icon in a rounded square
- Everything wrapped in cards; cards inside cards
- Same `rounded-2xl` and same shadow on every element
- Every section the same layout and the same vertical spacing
- Perfect symmetry everywhere — use asymmetry, overlaps, and a real grid
- 3-tier pricing with a "Most popular" badge when the product has no pricing
- Four-column footer full of dead links

### Icons
- Lucide icons (the default in shadcn) — use **Phosphor** (`@phosphor-icons/react`) or **Heroicons** (`@heroicons/react`) instead; pick one set and one weight per project
- Emoji used as icons
- An icon in a colored circle next to every single item

### Effects and motion
- Glassmorphism on everything
- Glow on hover, `scale-105` on every card hover
- Bounce or elastic easing
- Every element fading up on scroll with the same timing

### Content
- Fake logos ("Trusted by…"), fake testimonials, fake stats ("10,000+ users")
- Buzzwords: seamless, unleash, elevate, empower, revolutionize, supercharge, effortless, next-generation, cutting-edge
- Headlines like "Transform your X with AI"
- Abstract 3D shapes or generic illustrations in place of the real product

## 3. Do this instead

- **Fonts:** one display font with character plus a quiet body font. Sources: Google Fonts, Fontshare. Good starting pairs: Instrument Serif + Geist, Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans, Fraunces + Manrope, Clash Display + Satoshi, Newsreader + Inter Tight. Use big size contrast between heading and body.
- **Color:** one accent, tinted neutrals, lots of the background color. Take colors from a reference, not from Tailwind defaults.
- **Imagery:** real product screenshots in a browser/phone frame, real photos, or custom generated images. Never an empty illustration.
- **Layout:** vary sections — full-bleed image, split text/image, dense list, big number, quote. Let one element break the grid per page.
- **Copy:** specific and concrete. Say what the product does for whom, with real numbers from the project if there are any.
- **Components:** restyle shadcn components (radius, border, font, color) so they don't look like the stock shadcn demo.

## 4. Motion

Use the `motion` library (`motion/react`, formerly Framer Motion).
- Animate with purpose: page load of the hero, state changes, feedback on click. Not every element.
- Easing: ease-out curves or springs with no bounce (`type: "spring", bounce: 0`). Durations 150–400ms for UI, up to ~800ms for hero entrances.
- Stagger lists lightly (30–60ms), only for the first view.
- Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (`useReducedMotion`).

## 5. Before calling it done

1. Take screenshots at 1440px and 390px (Playwright if available) and look at them.
2. Check against the banned list above — fix every hit.
3. Audit by hand: text and control contrast (WCAG AA), visible focus rings, 44px touch
   targets, labels on every control, `prefers-reduced-motion`. Fix what fails, then polish
   spacing, alignment and copy.
4. Check hover, focus, empty, loading and error states, and mobile.

## Slides

Same rules: one theme, one accent, one display font, max ~15 words per slide, one real visual per slide, no gradient title slides.
